paper_metadata.title: Generative quantum learning of joint probability distribution functions

summary: The paper studies two gate-based quantum generative models for AAPL/MSFT daily-return copulas: a 6-qubit QGAN on IonQ trapped-ion hardware and a QCBM tested on 2, 4, 6, and 8 qubits across simulator, cloud QPU, and next-generation QPU. Reported metrics are modest: QGAN on hardware achieved DKS 0.0352 with p-value 0.3570, while QCBM on cloud QPU achieved DKS 0.0373–0.0515 with p-values 0.0548–0.3030; classical GAN and Gaussian-copula baselines remain competitive, so no practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: QGAN for learning the copula of daily returns of AAPL and MSFT using a 6-qubit qopula ansatz, evaluated on simulator and IonQ cloud trapped-ion hardware.

algorithm.ansatz: qopula circuit: Bell-pair entangling layer followed by one layer of parametrized single-qubit RZ/RX rotations and RXX entanglers
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initialization; for simulator and experiment comparison, same random seed used

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: angles optimized on [0, 2π] for random initialization in simulator runs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: daily returns transformed to copula space via probability integral transform; 3 qubits per variable used to represent discretized values, with additional 40 random bits appended after measurement to reduce discretization artifacts
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary cross-entropy GAN objective between real copula-space samples and generated copula-space samples
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: uniform marginals enforced by copula-space representation; no explicit penalty terms reported

problem_instance.description: Learning the joint distribution of two financial time series via copula modeling

dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily returns computed from adjacent close prices; probability integral transform to copula space

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: daily return r=(P2-P1)/P1; transform to uniform marginals using probability integral transform; reverse transform back to original space for visualization
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: trained on simulator and IonQ cloud QPU; convergence assessed by loss curves and 2D KS statistics; 2048 samples collected for evaluation

noise_model.noise_type: depolarizing noise up to 4% after each two-qubit gate in mixed-state simulation; hardware noise on IonQ cloud QPU

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: classical discriminator network; data transformed to copula space
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: generated copula samples transformed back to original space using inverse marginal CDFs; extra random bits appended to measured outputs
implementation_details.total_execution_time: QGAN experiment took 2 weeks to complete

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: generator and discriminator losses diverge initially then converge; KS statistic drops around convergence

speedup_claims.conditions: as stated in the paper's abstract; specific classical model details not fully quantified in the text
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is qualitative/summary-level; the paper does not provide a single controlled end-to-end iteration-count table for this exact comparison.

speedup_claims.factor: better stability and outperformance versus classical GAN with similar number of parameters
speedup_claims.conditions: AAPL/MSFT copula learning task on 6 qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: Performance is reported via KS statistics and p-values; no single scalar accuracy metric is used.

speedup_claims.factor: exponential classical hardness in worst case
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical simulation of qopula circuits / classical learning
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming the polynomial hierarchy does not collapse to the third level
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity-theoretic argument, not an end-to-end runtime benchmark for the full QGAN training pipeline.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: argued computational advantage via shallow circuits and sampling hardness; no explicit asymptotic runtime for QGAN training given
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: no explicit asymptotic runtime for classical GAN given; discussion argues classical simulation of qopula circuits would require exponential communication/time in worst case
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: classical GAN training reported as 6 minutes on CPU-only machine

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; experiments are at 6 qubits for QGAN and the paper argues future competitiveness around 50+ qubits.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 6-qubit trapped-ion QPU, 24 trainable parameters, 2048 shots per generator call, SPSA optimization, 1000 training iterations.
limiting_factors: Classical GAN baseline is competitive and sometimes close in KS metrics.
QPU runtime is long: QGAN experiment took 2 weeks.
No end-to-end asymptotic speedup is demonstrated for the learning task.
Advantage arguments are worst-case complexity arguments, not empirical advantage.

notes: Hardware type is reported as IonQ trapped-ion QPUs.
Circuit depth inferred as 1 layer from the one-layer ansatz description; the paper does not provide a transpiled depth.
Speedup order set to none_proven because the paper gives worst-case hardness arguments rather than a demonstrated end-to-end asymptotic speedup for the full learning task.
The paper reports QGAN DKS 0.0352 and p-value 0.3570 on IonQ cloud QPU, versus classical GAN DKS 0.0363–0.0508 and p-value 0.0530–0.309, but this is not a decisive practical advantage.
The authors claim better stability and fewer iterations, yet the classical baseline remains competitive and the paper does not establish a meaningful real-world speedup.

experiments.description: QCBM for learning the same AAPL/MSFT copula distribution using the qopula ansatz, evaluated on simulator, IonQ cloud QPU, and IonQ next-generation QPU across 2, 4, 6, and 8 qubits.

algorithm.ansatz: qopula circuit: Bell-pair entangling layer followed by one layer of parametrized single-qubit RZ/RX rotations and RXX entanglers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: training run of 200 iterations; minimum cost typically found within about 20 iterations for a=0.5,c=0.5
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initialized with optimal angles from the previous smaller system size (transfer learning)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: copula-space data binned into 2^(Nq/2) bins; measured bitstrings mapped to discretized values via linear transform and random-bit padding
problem_formulation.objective_function: KL divergence between target discrete copula distribution p and circuit output distribution q
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: uniform marginals in copula space; no explicit penalty terms reported

problem_instance.description: Learning the joint distribution of two financial time series via copula modeling

dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily returns computed from adjacent close prices; probability integral transform to copula space; binning into discrete distribution for KL objective

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: daily return r=(P2-P1)/P1; transform to copula space; bin into 2^(Nq/2) bins; append less significant random bits when generating samples
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20 iterations to reach minimum cost for some settings; 10 best minimum cost values averaged; 20 smallest measured cost values averaged; compared across simulator, cloud QPU, and next-gen QPU

hardware.device_name: IonQ cloud QPU; IonQ next-generation QPU

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise on IonQ QPUs; simulator results also discussed with finite-shot noise

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: copula-space binning; transfer learning initialization from smaller qubit instances
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: random bits appended to measured outputs to form finer-grained samples; KS metric used for evaluation
implementation_details.total_execution_time: 6 hours on cloud system for 6-qubit QCBM with 200 iterations; 5 hours on next-generation QPU

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: cost decreases with iterations; noisy hardware can reach lower cost early in optimization

speedup_claims.factor: about 2x shorter runtime on next-generation QPU vs cloud QPU
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper attributes this to increased stability and reduced runtime; it is not a universal speedup claim.

speedup_claims.factor: minimum cost found within about 20 iterations
speedup_claims.baseline_method: same QCBM with smaller SPSA step sizes / slower convergence
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a convergence observation, not a direct classical-vs-quantum speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: exponential classical hardness in worst case
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical simulation of qopula circuits / classical learning
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming the polynomial hierarchy does not collapse to the third level
speedup_claims.caveats: Complexity-theoretic argument only; not an end-to-end benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: no explicit asymptotic runtime for QCBM training given; paper argues shallow quantum circuits can be hard to classically simulate and may offer advantage for some distributions
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: classical simulation of the qopula-based learning task argued to require exponential time/communication in worst case
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: 5 hours on next-generation QPU for 6 qubits, 9 hours on cloud system for 6 qubits

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; results are reported for 2, 4, 6, and 8 qubits, with no demonstrated crossover to practical advantage.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Up to 8 qubits, 500 shots per circuit, SPSA optimization, 200 iterations, evaluated on simulator, cloud QPU, and next-generation QPU.
limiting_factors: Performance is comparable to classical GAN and only slightly better than the parametric baseline in some metrics.
No clear advantage over classical methods is demonstrated.
The paper notes noise can help early optimization, but this is not a scalable advantage.
Results are limited to small NISQ-scale systems.

notes: The paper reports results for 2, 4, 6, and 8 qubits; num_qubits is recorded as the maximum tested size (8) with scalability data across sizes.
Circuit depth inferred as 1 layer from the one-layer ansatz; transpiled depth not reported.
Speedup order set to none_proven because the paper provides theoretical hardness arguments but not a proven end-to-end asymptotic speedup for the full QCBM training task.
The QCBM achieves DKS 0.0425–0.0520 in simulation and 0.0373–0.0515 on cloud QPU, with p-values above 0.05, which is roughly on par with the classical GAN baseline rather than clearly superior.
The paper emphasizes that QCBM can converge in about 20 iterations for some settings, but does not establish a practical advantage.

experiments.description: Classical GAN baseline used to compare against QGAN/QCBM on the same AAPL/MSFT copula learning task.
key_results: About 40% of model instances were accepted by the 2D KS test at threshold 0.05.
Training used learning rate 0.0001 and concluded after 20000 iterations.

experiments.description: Parametric Gaussian copula baseline used for comparison on the same AAPL/MSFT copula task.
